params.body:
## Why the vehicle was null

Not a missing eager load, and not a rental created without a car: `RentalRequest::rules()`
makes `vehicle_id` required, so every rental has one.

The vehicle had been taken out of stock. `Vehicle` uses `SoftDeletes`, and `Rental::vehicle()`
was a plain `belongsTo` while its two siblings `Offer::vehicle()` and `Order::vehicle()` both
carry `->withTrashed()`. From the moment the dealer removed the car, the relation handed back
null and the document could not be opened at all, which is precisely the document you still
need then: it is the proof of the state the car left in.

`offertes/indexRentals.blade.php` survived because it does not use the relation. The repository
joins `vehicles` with a raw `leftJoin` (no soft-delete scope) and every cell is written as
`optional($rental?->vehicle?->manufacturer)->name`. Someone hardened the list, copied the two
guards into the heading of the document, and missed the third read. The guards were treating a
symptom that has a cause one layer down.

`rentals.vehicle_id` is nullable with no foreign key, so a vehicle row that is really gone
remains possible; that is the second case handled below.

## What the document now shows

- `Rental::vehicle()` carries `->withTrashed()`, like `Offer` and `Order`. A car that left the
  stock is simply on the document again, complete.
- If the vehicle row does not exist at all, the document still prints. The heading falls back to
  the licence plate, which the rental stores itself, and a line underneath says the vehicle is no
  longer in stock (`rental.vehicle_gone`, nl/en/fr/de).
- Every vehicle value that cannot be read reads "unknown" rather than an empty cell: an empty
  cell reads as zero kilometres or no colour, and not knowing is something else. What the rental
  recorded itself (plate, dates, mileage and fuel level at departure and return, signature page)
  is unaffected and keeps printing.

## What else in the template was unguarded

- `_tabs_bruikleen/general.blade.php`: the whole `@php` block (`kilowatt`, `horse_power`,
  `cylinder_capacity`) plus `mileage`, `color->name`, `fuel_type->name`,
  `transmission_type->name` and `chassis_number`. Only `initial_registration_date` was guarded.
- `bruikleen.blade.php`: `@if(!empty($rental->vehicle->damage))`, the gate in front of the damage
  include, read through the same null.
- `RentalController@show`: `PDF::SetTitle(...)` and `PDF::Output(...)` both built their string
  from `$rental->vehicle->manufacturer->name` and `$rental->vehicle->construction_year`. The
  template was only the first of three places to fall over.
- Deliberately left alone: `dealer_client_info.blade.php` and the sale point block read
  `$rental->relation->dealer->...` unguarded. That is a different relation and a different
  question, and adding `optional()` there as a reflex would hide it rather than answer it.

## The two sibling documents

Both carry the identical unguarded read at the heading, and in a slightly worse form: they do not
even use `?->` on the vehicle itself.

    offerte.blade.php:18    {{mb_strtoupper(optional($offer->vehicle->manufacturer)->name, ...)}} ... ({{$offer->vehicle->construction_year}})
    bestelbon.blade.php:19  {{mb_strtoupper(optional($order->vehicle->manufacturer)->name, ...)}} ... ({{$order->vehicle->construction_year}})

They do not crash on a removed car, because `Offer::vehicle()` and `Order::vehicle()` already
carry `withTrashed()`. They would crash on a vehicle row that is gone, and `offers.vehicle_id`
and `orders.vehicle_id` are both nullable. Both headings now use the same guarded form as the
rental, so a missing construction year no longer prints an empty bracket either. Nothing else in
those two documents was touched.

## Rules and tests

`R S4-9.7` is new in `docs/bedrijfsregels/14-s4-verkopen-aan-een-klant.md`: what the document
shows when the vehicle is gone. The defect is recorded as `X-124`.

`tests/Feature/RentalDocumentTest.php`, four tests tagged `@rule S4-9.7`: the vehicle in stock,
the vehicle soft-deleted (this one fails without the `withTrashed()`, checked by mutation), no
vehicle row at all, and the route itself answering with a pdf instead of a 500.

    vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='Rental|Bruikleen|Offer|Order|RulesCoverage'
    OK (75 tests, 292 assertions)
